HW 6


Exercise 1


a.	The most interesting lesson for me was the interaction of space and time in graphics especially the third example that mixes up space and time on the y axis which is really interesting because a graphic like that actually tells a story and makes it easier for viewers to infer what the purpose of the graph is.


b.  I would say my favorite graphic was on page 53.


![Favorite Graphic](/Screenshot 2026-02-18 175331.png)

  I picked this graphic because it is really simple to interpret but has some complex components and there is a good amount of detail in using the data as the data point. Very interesting and would be good for analogies when teaching.
  

The encoding channels used were position and shape! Position is associated with fear and rage. Shape is also associated with fear and rage.
It would definitely be hard to use the data(bear expressions) as datapoints/ as the marks.
Tufte was showing relational designs.


Exercise 2
•	Pages 81-90: Graphics that use bars should have a baseline for the best interpretation by the viewer.


•	Consistency of range of values on the x and y axes. Considering labeling data points instead of assigning multiple variables to one axis.


•	Important questions to ask yourself when designing a graphic:


o	What are you trying to show? How important is it? Who is your audience? Is your audience familiar with the type of graph? How are you presenting the information?


•	Reaching out for feedback and the perception of your graphic by viewers.


Exercise 3


```{r}
library(vegawidget)
'
{
  "$schema": "https://vega.github.io/schema/vega-lite/v5.json",
  "data": {
    "values": [
      {"Date": "Q1-2017", "Completion Rate": 0.91, "Response Rate": 0.023},
      {"Date": "Q2-2017", "Completion Rate": 0.93, "Response Rate": 0.018},
      {"Date": "Q3-2017", "Completion Rate": 0.91, "Response Rate": 0.028},
      {"Date": "Q4-2017", "Completion Rate": 0.89, "Response Rate": 0.023},
      {"Date": "Q1-2018", "Completion Rate": 0.84, "Response Rate": 0.034},
      {"Date": "Q2-2018", "Completion Rate": 0.88, "Response Rate": 0.027},
      {"Date": "Q3-2018", "Completion Rate": 0.91, "Response Rate": 0.026},
      {"Date": "Q4-2018", "Completion Rate": 0.87, "Response Rate": 0.039},
      {"Date": "Q1-2019", "Completion Rate": 0.83, "Response Rate": 0.028}
    ]
  },
  "repeat": {
    "row": ["Completion Rate", "Response Rate"]
  },
  "spec": {
    "width": 800,
    "height": 200,
    "title": "Completion and Response Rate through the Year Quarters",
    "mark": "bar",
    "encoding": {
      "x": {"field": "Date", "type": "ordinal", "title": "Quarter"},
      "y": {
        "field": {"repeat": "row"},
        "type": "quantitative",
        "title": "Rate"
      },
      "opacity": {"value": 0.7}
    }
  }
}
'|> as_vegaspec()
```



I paid attention to my data to mark ratio and made sure I made my graphic simple to interpret. I also made sure to let my bars start from a baseline of 0 to make interpretation easy and straightforward.
